common_name: Falling Stars Streptocarpus (Trailing Small-Flowered Cape Primrose)

planting.note: Divide crowded clumps or root leaf cuttings in spring; grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light in slightly acidic, well-drained, humus-rich potting mix. Falling Stars is a small-flowered, exceptionally floriferous trailing streptocarpus well suited to a hanging pot.

directions: Grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained, humus-rich potting mix, letting the top of the mix dry slightly between waterings. Falling Stars produces a profusion of small, star-shaped, pale lavender-blue flowers with a darker throat, held above a trailing mat of small, textured leaves, an especially floriferous small-flowered type well suited to a hanging basket where its cascading habit and abundant tiny blooms can be shown off. It blooms nearly continuously through the growing season under good light and tolerates slightly cooler indoor temperatures than African violet, its close relative. Remove spent flower stems at the base to encourage continued bloom, and divide congested clumps every couple of years to maintain vigor.

common_name: Constant Nymph Streptocarpus (Historic Classic Violet-Blue Cape Primrose)

planting.note: Divide crowded clumps or root leaf cuttings in spring; grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light in slightly acidic, well-drained, humus-rich potting mix. Constant Nymph is a historic mid-twentieth-century hybrid credited with popularizing streptocarpus as a widely grown houseplant.

directions: Grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light — never direct sun — in slightly acidic, well-drained, humus-rich potting mix, letting the top of the mix dry slightly between waterings. Constant Nymph bears trumpet-shaped, deep violet-blue flowers with darker throat veining over long, strap-like, textured leaves, a historic hybrid bred at England's Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, in the mid-twentieth century that is widely credited with launching streptocarpus into mainstream houseplant popularity after its introduction. It blooms nearly continuously through the growing season under good light and tolerates slightly cooler indoor temperatures than African violet, its close relative. Remove spent flower stems at the base to encourage continued bloom, and divide congested clumps every couple of years to maintain vigor.
